sentences.text: The Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse recommended a national strategy to prevent child sexual abuse.
sentences.section: Creating child safe communities through prevention
sentences.support:
The Australian Government should establish a mechanism to oversee the development and 
implementation of a national strategy to prevent child sexual abuse.

sentences.text: The Commission recommended that institutions put children’s interests first and implement its Child Safe Standards, including child participation, suitable staff and child-focused complaint processes.
sentences.section: What makes institutions safer for children
sentences.support:
In order to achieve this, institutions should implement 
the Child Safe Standards identified by the Royal Commission.

sentences.text: It also recommended longer retention of abuse records and government funding for coordinated advocacy, counselling and support for survivors.
sentences.section: Records and recordkeeping; Dedicated community support services for victims and survivors
sentences.support:
The Australian Government and state and territory governments should fund dedicated 
community support services for victims and survivors in each jurisdiction

sentences.text: The Commission recommended five years of annual implementation reports from governments and major institutions.
sentences.support:
through five consecutive annual reports 
tabled before their respective parliaments.

findings.quote: All institutions should uphold the rights of the child.

The Australian Government should establish a mechanism to oversee the development and 
implementation of a national strategy to prevent child sexual abuse.

notes: This is a recommendations compilation, including recommendations from earlier reports, without an executive summary, terms of reference or narrative findings. No overall recommendation total is stated here.
